comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13007#issuecomment-5790671461), checked at [`290d0ede`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/commit/290d0edee204a9d13432a475e1afd0600a24e59b) after [the author's update](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13007#issuecomment-5804904765).

**Outcome:** the earlier finding (fixed QWERTY positions change the shortcut on other Latin layouts) is **resolved**. Two narrower, configuration-specific issues remain in the new resolver, plus a robustness gap when the user's Compose file is broken.

## Earlier finding: resolved

**Verified:** the resolver now asks `xkbcli how-to-type` which key produces each letter in layout 1 of the configured keymap. Layout 1 is the right reference: Hyprland 0.56.2 [sends the injected key with modifier group 0](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f/src/config/shared/actions/ConfigActions.cpp#L1530-L1576), so applications read it in the first layout whichever layout is active.

| Layout / action | Previous head | This revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dvorak (`us,ru`, `dvorak,`): copy / paste / cut | code 54 / 55 / 53 (Ctrl+J / K / Q) | code 31 / 60 / 56 (Ctrl+C / V / X) |
| French AZERTY (`fr,ru`): select all | code 38 (Ctrl+Q) | code 24 (Ctrl+A) |
| Terminal copy / paste on Dvorak | Ctrl+Shift+J / K | Ctrl+Shift+C / V |

**Verified** in sandboxed runs with real `xkbcli` 1.13.2 and XKB data:

- The PR's parser also resolves A/C/V/X to 38/54/55/53 for the #12570 setup (`gb,ru,ua`), Omarchy's default `us,ru` form, `de,ru` and `us,dk,eu`. `code:N` skips the active-group lookup that raises `send_key_state: key not found`.
- `xkbcli` runs once per letter, then the result is cached. Without `xkbcli`, the named keys are sent with no Lua error.
- The repository test passes on this head. With this head's test copied onto the base, it fails at the select-all check; on the previous head, it fails at the Dvorak copy check. So the new checks do guard the earlier finding.

## Per-device keymaps and `kb_file` are ignored

The resolver reads only the global `input.kb_*` values ([`clipboard.lua`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/290d0edee204a9d13432a475e1afd0600a24e59b/default/hypr/bindings/clipboard.lua#L50-L96)). Hyprland builds each keyboard's keymap from that device's own `kb_*` overrides or `kb_file` ([`InputManager.cpp`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f/src/managers/input/InputManager.cpp#L1218-L1231), [`IKeyboard.cpp`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/efb50993780079460b0cbed1363e2166a2de1d9f/src/devices/IKeyboard.cpp#L67-L102)), and sends applications the active keyboard's keymap.

Source-traced example, not run in a compositor:

```text
global kb_layout = "us"; external keyboard: kb_variant = "dvorak"
SUPER+C on that keyboard
  resolver (global us)  -> code:54
  application (Dvorak)  -> reads code 54 as J -> Ctrl+J
  base (named key C)    -> resolved on the active keyboard -> Ctrl+C
```

A global `input.kb_file` whose layout moves A/C/V/X behaves the same way.

**Impact:** on setups with a per-device layout or a custom keymap file, the earlier finding's symptom returns: the shortcut sends a different letter. The default global `us,ru` setup is not affected.

**Suggested change:** fall back to the named key when `input.kb_file` is set, and document or handle per-device overrides. Hyprland's Lua `hl.get_config` returns global values only, so a full fix may need a Hyprland-side API.

## Letter matched at any shift level

The parser takes the first layout-1 line for the uppercase letter at any level. In `us(3l)`, `us(3l-cros)` and `us(3l-emacs)`, key 30 carries `A` at level 6 and sorts before the real A key (41). SUPER+A then sends Ctrl+K instead of Ctrl+A; the base sent the correct key. A scan of all 753 layout/variant pairs found only these three where the choice changes a previously working chord.

**Impact:** select-all sends Ctrl+K on those three variants.

**Suggested change:** look up the lowercase letter (`key:lower()`) and accept only lines whose level column is 1, which matches how applications and Hyprland's own named-key lookup read the key.

## A broken Compose file silently disables the resolver

From libxkbcommon 1.11, `how-to-type` loads the user's Compose file by default. If that file opens but fails to parse (for example, an `include` pointing to a missing file), it exits with no output. The resolver discards stderr, caches the named-key fallback and reuses it until the Lua config reloads or the `input.kb_*` values change. This is not a regression: the fallback is the base behavior. A healthy Omarchy Compose setup was not affected in testing.

**Impact:** on a system with a damaged or stale Compose file, #12570 stays unfixed for that session, with no diagnostic.

**Suggested change:** pass `--disable-compose`, since only the direct keymap rows are needed. Versions before 1.11 reject that flag, so older libxkbcommon would need a retry without it.
